lines.text: 10 times the Sun's mass. Only 60 km wide.
You can't see it. Only stars bending around it.
You don't feel its pull. Earth falls with you.
But the near side is pulled harder. The tides rise.
Twice a day, the sea climbs higher.
40 million km: the Moon is ripped away.
It shreds into a disk, millions of degrees hot.
Tides of 5 km. The ground itself stretches.
1.2 million km: its tides match Earth's gravity.
On this side of Earth, nothing weighs anything.
Every piece falls into the disk and burns.
Past the event horizon, even light can't escape.
No one would ever see Earth again.
